[[Kingdom of Denmark|Denmark]] first participated at the [[Olympic Games]] at the inaugural 1896 Games. Since then, the nation has maintained a consistent presence at the [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympics]], participating in every edition except for the [[1904 Summer Olympics|1904 Games]] in [[St. Louis]], which were attended by only a handful of countries due to travel difficulties and limited international participation. Denmark has also participated in the [[Winter Olympic Games]] several times since 1948, including every Games since 1988.

Danish athletes have competed across a wide range of sports, with [[Sailing (sport)|sailing]] emerging as the country's most successful discipline in terms of medal achievements. Other sports in which Denmark has performed well include [[Cycle sport|cycling]], [[Rowing (sport)|rowing]], [[handball]] (leading nation at the Olympics), and [[badminton]]—the latter gaining prominence in recent decades.
While the country does not have a strong tradition in winter sports compared to its summer achievements, it secured its first Winter Olympic medal at the [[1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Nagano Games]], where the [[curling at the 1998 Winter Olympics|women's curling team]] won a silver medal, marking a historic moment for Danish winter sports.<ref name="DEN_profile">{{cite web | url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/denmark | title=Denmark - NOC Profile | website=olympics.com| publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) | date=2024 |access-date=2024-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042823/https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/denmark |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In addition to its sporting achievements, Denmark have won medals in one of the three discontinued [[Olympic sports#Feats and artistic events|Olympic non-sport competitions]], winning five silver and four bronze medals at the [[Art competitions at the Summer Olympics|art competitions]].<ref name="DEN_profile" />

The [[National Olympic Committee and Sports Confederation of Denmark|National Olympic Committee]] representing Denmark, known as Danmarks Idrætsforbund, was established in 1905, playing a central role in organizing Denmark's Olympic efforts and supporting its athletes across both Summer and Winter Games.

== List of medalists ==
=== Athletes with most medals ===
According to official data of the [[International Olympic Committee]], this is a list of Danish athletes who have won two or more Olympic gold medals or three or more Olympic medals with at least one gold medal and one silver medal. Medals won in the [[1906 Intercalated Games]] are not included. It includes top-three placings in 1896 and 1900, before medals were awarded for top-three placings.

=== Medals by team ===
Denmark has been successful at the Olympics in team sports like [[Association football|football]], [[Team handball|handball]] and team [[gymnastics]]. In football [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] has won four medals. Also team gymnastics has given Denmark four medals. In women's handball [[Denmark women's national handball team|Denmark]] has won three gold medals.

=== Summer Olympics ===
All Danish medals are listed.

==Summary by summer sport==

===Non-participations===
Denmark has participated in most summer sports, but they have yet to participate in: [[Artistic swimming at the Summer Olympics|Artistic swimming]], [[Baseball at the Summer Olympics|Baseball]]/[[Softball at the Summer Olympics|Softball]], [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Basketball]], [[Cricket at the Summer Olympics|Cricket]], [[Lacrosse at the Summer Olympics|Lacrosse]], [[Rugby football]] (neither [[Rugby sevens at the Summer Olympics|Rugby sevens]] or the discontinued discipline [[Rugby union at the Summer Olympics|Rugby union]]), [[Sport climbing at the Summer Olympics|Sport climbing]], [[Surfing at the Summer Olympics|Surfing]], [[Volleyball at the Summer Olympics|Volleyball]] and [[Water polo at the Summer Olympics|Water polo]].

Denmark never participated in the following discontinued sports: [[Basque pelota at the 1900 Summer Olympics|Basque pelota]], [[Croquet at the 1900 Summer Olympics|Croquet]], [[Jeu de paume at the 1908 Summer Olympics|Jeu de paume]], [[Karate at the Summer Olympics|Karate]], [[Polo at the Summer Olympics|Polo]], [[Rackets at the 1908 Summer Olympics|Rackets]], [[Roque at the 1904 Summer Olympics|Roque]] and [[Water motorsports at the 1908 Summer Olympics|Water motorsports]].

===Aquatics===
For aquatics disciplines, follow these links: [[#Diving|Diving]] and [[#Swimming|Swimming]].

Denmark has yet to participate in [[Artistic swimming at the Summer Olympics|Artistic swimming]] and [[Water polo at the Summer Olympics|Water polo]].

===[[Archery at the Summer Olympics|Archery]]===
Archery was included in the Olympic programme four times between 1900 and 1920. It returned in 1972 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 8th by [[Arne Jacobsen (archer)|Arne Jacobsen]] in [[Archery at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's individual|men's individual in 1972]]. That result was matched by [[Carina Christiansen]], [[Maja Jager]] and [[Louise Laursen]] in [[Archery at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's team|women's team in 2012]].

===[[Athletics at the Summer Olympics|Athletics]]===
Athletics has been included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympics.

Denmark has won 7 medals in athletics; 4 silver and 3 bronze.

Their most successful athlete in the sport is [[Wilson Kipketer]] who competed in men's 800m, winning silver in [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres|2000]] and bronze in [[Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres|2004]].

Denmark's most successful female athlete in the sport is [[Sara Slott Petersen]] who won silver in [[Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metres hurdles|women's 400m hurdles in 2016]].

Denmark's remaining silver medalists are [[Henry Petersen]] who won his medal in [[Athletics at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's pole vault|men's pole vault in 1920]] and [[Joachim Olsen]] who won his medal in [[Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's shot put|men's shot put in 2004]].

===[[Badminton at the Summer Olympics|Badminton]]===
Badminton has been included in the Olympic programme since 1992. Denmark has participated in every event held in the sport.

Denmark has been quite successful in the sport, winning 2 gold, 3 silver and 4 bronze medals.

[[Viktor Axelsen]] won gold in [[Badminton at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|men's singles in 2020]] and bronze in the same event in [[Badminton at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2016]].

[[Poul-Erik Høyer Larsen]] won gold in [[Badminton at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|men's singles in 1996]].

Denmark's most successful female athlete is [[Christinna Pedersen]] who won silver in [[Badminton at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|women's doubles in 2016]] together with [[Kamilla Rytter Juhl]], and won bronze in [[Badminton at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|mixed doubles in 2012]] together with [[Joachim Fischer Nielsen]].

===[[Boxing at the Summer Olympics|Boxing]]===
Boxing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1904 with the exception of 1912.

Denmark has won a total of 12 medals in the sport; 1 gold, 5 silver and 6 bronze.

[[Hans Jacob Nielsen]] won their only Olympic title in the sport by winning [[Boxing at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Lightweight|men's lightweight in 1924]].

[[Søren Petersen]] is their only double medalist in the sport, winning silver in men's heavyweight in both [[Boxing at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Heavyweight|1920]] and [[Boxing at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Heavyweight|1924]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the sport.

===[[Canoeing at the Summer Olympics|Canoeing]]===
====[[Canoeing at the Summer Olympics#Canoe slalom|Slalom]]====
Canoe slalom was first included in the Olympic programme in 1972. It returned in 1992 and has remained in the programme since then.

Denmark has yet to participate in the discipline.

====[[Canoeing at the Summer Olympics#Canoe sprint|Sprint]]====
Canoe sprint (including the discontinued discipline canoe marathon) has been included in the Olympic programme since 1936. Denmark has participated in the discipline every time it has been included in the programme.

Denmark has had some success in the discipline, winning 3 gold, 6 silver and 7 bronze medals.

Their most successful canoeist is [[Erik Hansen (canoeist)|Erik Hansen]] who won gold in [[Canoeing at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 1000 metres|men's K1 1000m in 1960]] and bronze medals in [[Canoeing at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 4 × 500 metres|men's K1x4 500m in 1960]] (together with [[Arne Høyer]], [[Erling Jessen]] and [[Helmuth Sørensen]]) and [[Canoeing at the 1968 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 1000 metres|men's K1 1000m in 1968]].

Denmark's remaining Olympic champions are [[Karen Hoff]] who won [[Canoeing at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's K-1 500 metres|women's K1 500m in 1948]] and [[Finn Haunstoft]] & [[Bent Peder Rasch]] who won [[Canoeing at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Men's C-2 1000 metres|men's C2 1000m in 1952]].

The female Danish canoeist with most medals is [[Emma Jørgensen]] who won silver in [[Canoeing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's K-1 500 metres|women's K1 500m in 2016]] and bronze in both [[Canoeing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's K-1 200 metres|K1 200m]] and [[Canoeing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's K-1 500 metres|K1 500m]] in 2020.

===[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics|Cycling]]===
====[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics#BMX freestyle|BMX freestyle]]====
BMX freestyle has been included in the Olympic programme since 2020. Denmark has yet to participate in the discipline.

====[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics#BMX racing|BMX racing]]====
BMX racing has been included in the Olympic programme since 2008.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 6th by [[Simone Christensen]] in [[Cycling at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's BMX racing|women's BMX racing in 2020]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the discipline was 19th by [[Morten Therkildsen]] in [[Cycling at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's BMX|men's BMX in 2012]]. [[Henrik Baltzersen]] ranked similarly in the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's BMX|men's BMX in 2008]], but cyclists eliminated in the heats weren't given an overall ranking then.

====[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics#Mountain biking|Mountain biking]]====
Mountain biking has been included in the Olympic programme since 1996.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 7th by [[Lennie Kristensen]] in [[Cycling at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's cross-country|men's cross-country in 1996]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the discipline was 11th by [[Annika Langvad]] in [[Cycling at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's cross-country|women's cross-country in 2016]].

====[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics#Road cycling|Road cycling]]====
Road cycling was included in the Olympic programme in 1896. It returned in 1912 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since. Denmark has participated in the discipline every Games since 1912.

Denmark has won 2 gold, 5 silver and 1 bronze medal in the discipline.

Their most successful road cyclist was [[Henry Hansen (cyclist)|Henry Hansen]] who won gold in [[Cycling at the 1928 Summer Olympics – Men's individual time trial|men's individual time trial]] and [[Cycling at the 1928 Summer Olympics – Men's team time trial|men's team time trial]] (together with [[Orla Jørgensen]] and [[Leo Nielsen]]) in 1928, and silver in [[Cycling at the 1932 Summer Olympics – Men's team time trial|men's team time trial in 1932]] (together with Leo Nielsen again but also [[Frode Sørensen (cyclist)|Frode Sørensen]]).

[[Leo Nielsen]] is the second most successful Danish cyclists in the discipline with his 1 gold and 1 silver mentioned above.

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the discipline was 5th by [[Linda Villumsen]] in [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's individual road race|women's individual road race in 2008]].

====[[Cycling at the Summer Olympics#Track cycling|Track cycling]]====
Track cycling was included in the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympic programme and has been included in all Summer Games except for 1912.

Denmark has obtained 21 medals in the discipline, 6 gold, 6 silver and 9 bronze.

Their most successful track cyclist is [[Lasse Norman Hansen]] with 2 gold, 1 silver and 2 bronze medals. He won his Olympic titles in [[Cycling at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's omnium|men's omnium in 2012]] and [[Cycling at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's Madison|men's Madison in 2020]], the latter together with [[Michael Mørkøv]].

Denmark has two more track cyclists with 3 medals. [[Willy Falck Hansen]] won 1 gold, 1 silver and 1 bronze. His Olympic title came in [[Cycling at the 1928 Summer Olympics – Men's track time trial|men's time trial in 1928]]. [[Niels Fredborg]] also won 1 gold, 1 silver and 1 bronze. His Olympic title came in [[Cycling at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's track time trial|men's time trial in 1972]].

Denmark's most successful female track cyclists are [[Amalie Dideriksen]] and [[Julie Leth]] who won silver together in [[Cycling at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's Madison|women's Madison in 2020]].

===[[Diving at the Summer Olympics|Diving]]===
Diving has been included in the Olympic programme since 1904.

Denmark has won two medals in the sport, a gold and a bronze. [[Stefanie Clausen]] won gold in [[Diving at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Women's 10 metre platform|women's 10m platform in 1920]]. [[Birte Christoffersen]] won bronze in [[Diving at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's 10 metre platform|women's 10m platform in 1948]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the sport was 6th, a record shared between [[Herold Jansson]] in [[Diving at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's plain high diving|men's plain high diving in 1920]] and [[Thomas Christiansen]] in [[Diving at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Men's 10 metre platform|men's 10m platform in 1948]].

===[[Equestrian at the Summer Olympics|Equestrian]]===
====Dressage====
Dressage had one event included in 1900. It returned to the Olympic programme in 1912 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since.

Denmark has won 4 medals in the sport; 3 silver and 1 bronze.

[[Lis Hartel]] won silver in the individual event both in [[Equestrian at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Individual dressage|1952]] and [[Equestrian at the 1956 Summer Olympics – Individual dressage|1956]]. [[Anne Grethe Jensen]] also earned silver in the individual event, in [[Equestrian at the 1984 Summer Olympics – Individual dressage|1984]].

Their bronze medal was won by [[Andreas Helgstrand]], [[Anne van Olst]] and [[Princess Nathalie of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg]] in the [[Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Team dressage|team event in 2008]].

====Eventing====
Eventing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1912.

Denmark has won two medals in the discipline, a silver and a bronze. [[Frode Kirkebjerg]] won silver in [[Equestrian at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Individual eventing|individual eventing in 1924]] and [[Hans Lunding]] won bronze in the same event in [[Equestrian at the 1936 Summer Olympics – Individual eventing|1936]].

Denmark has yet to send female riders to compete in the discipline.

====Show jumping====
Show Jumping was included in the Olympic programme in 1900. It returned in 1912 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since.

Denmark's best placement in the discipline was 8th by [[Merethe Jensen]] in the [[Equestrian at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Individual jumping|individual event in 1992]].

Denmark's best placement by a male rider in the discipline was shared 10th by [[Thomas Velin]] in the individual event in both [[Equestrian at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Individual jumping|2000]] and [[Equestrian at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Individual jumping|2004]].

====Discontinued disciplines====
Equestrian driving was conducted during the [[1900 Summer Olympics]] and equestrian vaulting during the [[1920 Summer Olympics]]. Denmark did not participate in the disciplines.

===[[Fencing at the Summer Olympics|Fencing]]===
Fencing has been included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1896 Games.

Denmark has won six medals in the sport, 1 gold, 2 silver and 3 bronze.

Their Olympic gold was won by [[Ellen Osiier]] in [[Fencing at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Women's foil|women's foil in 1924]]. [[Grete Heckscher]] won bronze in the same event.

[[Karen Lachmann]] is the Danish fencer with most medals as she won silver in [[Fencing at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's foil|women's foil in 1948]] and bronze in the [[Fencing at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Women's foil|same event in 1952]].

Two Danish men have earned medals. [[Ivan Osiier]] won silver in [[Fencing at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's épée|men's épée in 1912]] and [[Holger Nielsen]] won bronze in [[Fencing at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's sabre|men's sabre in 1896]].

===[[Field hockey at the Summer Olympics|Field hockey]]===
Field hockey was first included in the Olympic programme in 1908. It returned in 1920 before becoming a permanent Olympic sport in 1928.

Denmark only medal so far is the silver [[Denmark men's national field hockey team]] won in [[Field hockey at the 1920 Summer Olympics|1920]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the sport.

===[[Football at the Summer Olympics|Football]]===
Football has been included in the Olympic programme since 1900 with the exception of 1932.¨

Denmark has won four medals so far, [[Denmark men's national football team]] won silver medals in [[Football at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]], [[Football at the 1912 Summer Olympics|1912]] and [[Football at the 1960 Summer Olympics|1960]] and a bronze medal in [[Football at the 1948 Summer Olympics|1948]].

Six Danish footballers won two silver medals, [[Charles Buchwald]], [[Harald Hansen (footballer)|Harald Hansen]], [[Nils Middelboe]], [[Oscar Nielsen]], [[Sophus Nielsen]] and [[Vilhelm Wolfhagen]] were all part of the teams in both 1908 and 1912.

[[Denmark women's national football team]]'s best placement is [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|8th in 1996]].

===[[Golf at the Summer Olympics|Golf]]===
Golf was included in the Olympic programme in 1900 and 1904. It returned in 2016 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was shared 5th by [[Emily Pedersen]] in [[Golf at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's individual|women's individual in 2020]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the sport was shared 21st by [[Søren Kjeldsen]] in [[Golf at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's individual|men's individual in 2016]].

===[[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics|Gymnastics]]===
====[[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics#Artistic gymnastics|Artistic gymnastics]]====
Artistic gymnastics has been included in the Summer Olympic programme since the inaugural 1896 Games.

Denmark has won four medals in the discipline. They won gold in gold in [[Gymnastics at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's team, free system|men's team free system in 1920]], silver in men's team Swedish system in [[Gymnastics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's team, Swedish system|1912]] and [[Gymnastics at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's team, Swedish system|1920]] and a bronze in [[Gymnastics at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's team, free system|men's team free system in 1912]].

The only multi medalists were [[Steen Olsen]] who participated in the free system in both 1912 and 1920 (winning bronze and gold respectively) and [[Hans Pedersen]] who participated in the Swedish system in both 1912 and 1920, winning silver both times.

Their best placement in a women's event in the sport was shared 62nd by [[Else Trangbæk]] in [[Gymnastics at the 1968 Summer Olympics – Women's balance beam|women's balance beam in 1968]].

Denmark also won a silver medal in artistic gymnastics at the [[1906 Intercalated Games]]. IOC has retroactively decided to no longer recognize those games as official Olympic games.

====[[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics#Rhythmic gymnastics|Rhythmic gymnastics]]====
Rhythmic gymnastics has been included in the Olympic programme since 1984.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 34th by [[Malene Franzen]] in [[Gymnastics at the 1988 Summer Olympics – Women's rhythmic individual all-around|women's rhythmic individual all-around in 1988]].

No men's events are held in the discipline.

====[[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics#Trampoline|Trampoline]]====
Trampoline has been included in the Olympic programme since 2000.

Denmark's best placement in the discipline was 10th by [[Peter Jensen (gymnast)|Peter Jensen]]. He obtained that placement in men's trampoline in both [[Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's trampoline|2008]] and [[Gymnastics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's trampoline|2012]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the discipline.

===[[Handball at the Summer Olympics|Handball]]===
Handball was included in the Olympic programme in 1936. It returned in 1972 and has remained in the Olympic programme ever since.

Denmark has won 5 medals in the sport, 4 gold and 1 silver. [[Denmark women's national handball team]] won gold in the women's events in [[Handball at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|1996]], [[Handball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2000]] and [[Handball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2004]]. [[Denmark men's national handball team]] won gold in the men's event in [[Handball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016]] and silver in [[Handball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020]].

12 Danish handballers are double Olympic champions; [[Camilla Andersen]], [[Tina Bøttzau]], [[Anette Hoffmann]], [[Tonje Kjærgaard]], [[Janne Kolling]] and [[Lene Rantala]] won gold with the women's team in 1996 and 2000, while [[Karen Brødsgaard]], [[Katrine Fruelund]], [[Lotte Kiærskou]], [[Karin Mortensen]], [[Rikke Petersen-Schmidt]] and [[Mette Vestergaard]] won gold in 2000 and 2004.

Denmark's most successful male handballers are [[Henrik Toft Hansen]], [[Mikkel Hansen]], [[Niklas Landin]], [[Mads Mensah Larsen]], [[Henrik Møllgaard]], [[Morten Olsen]] and [[Lasse Svan Hansen]] who won gold in 2016 and silver in 2020 with the men's team.

===[[Judo at the Summer Olympics|Judo]]===
Judo has been included in the Olympic programme since 1964 with the exception of the 1968 Games.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 11th by [[Tommy Mortensen]] in [[Judo at the 1988 Summer Olympics – Men's 65 kg|men's 65 kg in 1988]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was shared 17th by [[Lærke Olsen]] in [[Judo at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 63 kg|women's 63 kg in 2020]].

===[[Modern pentathlon at the Summer Olympics|Modern pentathlon]]===
Modern pentathlon has been included in the Olympic programme since 1912.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 5th by [[Marius Christensen]] in [[Modern pentathlon at the 1920 Summer Olympics|men's individual in 1920]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was 19rd by [[Pernille Svarre]] in [[Modern pentathlon at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's|women's individual in 2000]].

===[[Rowing at the Summer Olympics|Rowing]]===
Rowing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1900.

Denmark has won 7 gold, 5 silver and 13 bronze medals for a total medal count of 25 in the sport.

Denmark's most successful rower is [[Eskild Ebbesen]] who won three gold medals and two bronze medals in men's lightweight coxless four. He won his Olympic titles in [[Rowing at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's lightweight coxless four|1996]] (together with [[Victor Feddersen]], [[Niels Henriksen]] and [[Thomas Poulsen]]), [[Rowing at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's lightweight coxless four|2004]] (together with [[Thomas Ebert]], [[Stephan Mølvig]] and [[Thor Kristensen]]) and [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's lightweight coxless four|2008]] (together with [[Mads Andersen (rower)|Mads Andersen]], Thomas Ebert and [[Morten Jørgensen]]).

[[Thomas Ebert]] who was present for two of those Olympic titles, and also won a bronze medal, is Denmark's second most successful rower.

Denmark's most successful female rower is [[Fie Udby Erichsen]] who won silver in [[Rowing at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's single sculls|women's single sculls in 2012]].

===[[Sailing at the Summer Olympics|Sailing]]===
Sailing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1900 with the exception of 1904.

Denmark has been highly successful in the sport, winning 31 medals of which 13 are gold.

Their most successful athlete in the sport is [[Paul Elvstrøm]] who won four Olympic titles; [[Sailing at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Firefly|Firefly in 1948]] and Finn in [[Sailing at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Finn|1952]], [[Sailing at the 1956 Summer Olympics – Finn|1956]] and [[Sailing at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Finn|1960]].

Denmark also has four double Olympic champions. 
[[Valdemar Bandolowski]], [[Erik Hansen (sailor)|Erik Hansen]] and [[Poul Richard Høj Jensen]] won the Soling class together in [[Sailing at the 1976 Summer Olympics – Soling|1976]] and [[Sailing at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Soling|1980]].

[[Jesper Bank]] won the Soling class in [[Sailing at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Soling|1992]] with [[Steen Secher]] and [[Jesper Seier]] and again in [[Sailing at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Soling|2000]], then with [[Henrik Blakskjær]] and [[Thomas Jacobsen (sailor)|Thomas Jacobsen]].

Their most successful female athlete in the sport is [[Anne-Marie Rindom]] who won gold in [[Sailing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Laser Radial|Laser Radial in 2020]] after earning bronze in [[Sailing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Laser Radial|the same event in 2016]].

===[[Shooting at the Summer Olympics|Shooting]]===
Shooting was included in the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympic programme and has been included in all Summer Games except for 1904 and 1928. Denmark has participated in the sport every time except for 1932.

Denmark most successful shooter was [[Lars Jørgen Madsen]] who won 5 medals; 2 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze. His Olympic titles came in [[Shooting at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's 300 metre free rifle, standing|standing military rifle in 1900]] and in [[Shooting at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's 300 metre team military rifle, standing|men's 300m team military rifle standing]], the latter together with [[Niels Larsen]], [[Anders Peter Nielsen]], [[Anders Petersen (sport shooter)|Anders Petersen]] and [[Erik Sætter-Lassen]].

Anders Peter Nielsen mentioned above is Denmark's second most successful shooter, as he also won three silver medals on top of his gold.

Denmark's remaining Olympic champion in the sport is [[Kjeld Rasmussen]] who won gold in [[Shooting at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Mixed skeet|mixed skeet in 1980]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport is 6th by [[Anni Bissø]] in [[Shooting at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre rifle three positions|women's 50m rifle 3 positions in 2000]].

===[[Skateboarding at the Summer Olympics|Skateboarding]]===
Skateboarding has been included in the Olympic programme since 2020.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 19th by [[Rune Glifberg]] in [[Skateboarding at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's park|men's park in 2020]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the sport.

===[[Swimming at the Summer Olympics|Swimming]]===
====[[Swimming at the Summer Olympics#Long course swimming|Long course swimming]]====
Long course swimming has been included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympics.

Denmark first competed in swimming in 1900. They have won 15 medals in all, 3 gold, 5 silver and 7 bronze.

Denmark's most successful swimmer is [[Karen Harup]] who won gold in [[Swimming at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre backstroke|women's 100m backstroke]] and silver in both [[Swimming at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metre freestyle|women's 400m freestyle]] and [[Swimming at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay|women's {{nowrap|4 × 100 m}} freestyle relay]] (the latter together with [[Greta Andersen]], [[Eva Arndt]] and [[Fritze Carstensen]]), all in 1948.

Aside from winning a silver medal in that relay, [[Greta Andersen]] also won gold in [[Swimming at the 1948 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle|women's 100m freestyle in 1948]].

Denmark's remaining gold medal was won by [[Pernille Blume]] in [[Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle|women's 50m freestyle in 2016]]. She also won bronze in [[Swimming at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle|the same event in 2020]] and in [[Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay|women's {{nowrap|4 × 100 m}} medley relay in 2016]] (together with [[Rikke Møller Pedersen]], [[Mie Nielsen]] and [[Jeanette Ottesen]]).

The most successful male Danish swimmer were [[Ludvig Dam]] who won silver in [[Swimming at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre backstroke|men's 100m backstroke in 1908]] and [[Benny Nielsen (swimmer)|Benny Nielsen]] who won silver in [[Swimming at the 1988 Summer Olympics – Men's 200 metre butterfly|men's 200m butterfly in 1988]].

====[[Swimming at the Summer Olympics#Marathon swimming|Marathon swimming]]====
Marathon swimming has been included in the Olympic programme since 2008. Denmark has yet to participate in the discipline.

===[[Table tennis at the Summer Olympics|Table tennis]]===
Table tennis has been included in the Olympic programme since 1988.

Denmark has won one medal in the sport; [[Michael Maze]] and [[Finn Tugwell]] won bronze in [[Table tennis at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles|men's doubles in 2004]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was shared 33rd by [[Mie Skov]] in [[Table tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's singles|women's singles in 2012]].

===[[Taekwondo at the Summer Olympics|Taekwondo]]===
Taekwondo has been included in the Olympic programme since 2000.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 4th by [[Hanne Høegh Poulsen]] in [[Taekwondo at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 49 kg|women's 49 kg in 2000]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the sport was shared 9th by [[Jesper Roesen]] in [[Taekwondo at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 68 kg|men's 68 kg in 2004]].

===[[Tennis at the Summer Olympics|Tennis]]===
Tennis was originally included in the Olympic programme between 1896 and 1924. Tennis returned to the games in 1988 and has remained in the programme since then.

Denmark has won one medal in the sport; [[Sofie Castenschiold]] won silver in [[Tennis at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Women's indoor singles|women's indoor singles in 1912]].

Denmark's best placement by a male athlete in the sport is 4th, which [[Erik Tegner]] accomplished together with [[Amory Hansen]] in [[Tennis at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|mixed doubles in 1920]].

===[[Triathlon at the Summer Olympics|Triathlon]]===
Triathlon has been included in the Olympic programme since 2000.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 7th by [[Rasmus Henning]] in [[Triathlon at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's|men's individual in 2004]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was 23rd by [[Line Jensen (triathlete)|Line Jensen]] in [[Triathlon at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's|women's individual in 2012]].

===[[Tug of war at the Summer Olympics|Tug of war]]===
Tug of war was included in the Olympic programme between 1900 and 1920.

Denmark never participated as a separate team, but in 1900, three Danish and three Swedish athletes teamed up and [[Tug of war at the 1900 Summer Olympics|won the gold medal as a mixed team]].

The three Danish Olympic champions in tug of war were [[Edgar Aabye]], [[Eugen Schmidt]] and [[Charles Winckler]].

===[[Weightlifting at the Summer Olympics|Weightlifting]]===
Weightlifting was first included in the Olympic programme at the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympics. It was excluded from the 1900, 1908 and 1912 Games but have been included every other time.

Denmark has won three medals in the sport, 1 gold and 2 silver. They first competed in weightlifting at the inaugural 1896 Games, with one lifter competing. [[Viggo Jensen]] won gold in the [[Weightlifting at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's two hand lift|men's two-hand lift]] (based on a style tie-breaker), but was injured in the attempt and placed second for silver in [[Weightlifting at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's one hand lift|men's one-hand lift]].

Denmark's remaining silver medal was won by [[Svend Olsen]] in [[Weightlifting at the 1932 Summer Olympics – Men's 82.5 kg|men's 82.5 kg in 1932]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the sport.

===[[Wrestling at the Summer Olympics|Wrestling]]===
Wrestling was included in the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympic programme and has been included in all Summer Games except for 1900.

Denmark has won 9 medals in the sport, 3 silver and 6 bronze.

Their silver medals were won by [[Poul Hansen (sport wrestler)|Poul Hansen]] in [[Wrestling at the 1920 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman heavyweight|men's Greco-Roman heavyweight in 1920]], [[Abraham Kurland]] in [[Wrestling at the 1932 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman lightweight|men's Greco-Roman lightweight in 1932]] and [[Mark Madsen (fighter)|Mark Madsen]] in [[Wrestling at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman 75 kg|men's Greco-Roman 75 kg in 2016]].

The Danish wrestler with most Olympic medals is [[Søren Marinus Jensen]] who won 2 bronze medals, in men's Greco-Roman [[Wrestling at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman heavyweight|super heavyweight in 1908]] and [[Wrestling at the 1912 Summer Olympics – Men's Greco-Roman heavyweight|heavyweight in 1912]].

Denmark has yet to participate in women's events in the sport.

Denmark also won two gold medals, one silver medal and one bronze medal in wrestling at the [[1906 Intercalated Games]]. IOC has retroactively decided to no longer recognize those games as official Olympic games.

==Summary by winter sport==

===Non-participations===
Denmark has participated in most winter sports but has yet to participate in [[Luge at the Winter Olympics|Luge]], [[Nordic combined at the Winter Olympics|Nordic combined]], [[Short track speed skating at the Winter Olympics|Short track speed skating]] and [[Ski jumping at the Winter Olympics|Ski jumping]] and the temporary sport [[Ski mountaineering at the Winter Olympics|Ski Mountaineering]].

(They also didn't participate in [[Military patrol at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Military Patrol in 1924]], which sometimes is counted separately from Biathlon.)

===[[Alpine skiing at the Winter Olympics|Alpine skiing]]===
Alpine skiing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1936.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 20th by [[Christian Borgnæs]] in [[Alpine skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|men's giant slalom in 2026]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was 28th by [[Tine Kongsholm]] in [[Alpine skiing at the 1992 Winter Olympics – Women's slalom|women's slalom in 1992]].

===[[Biathlon at the Winter Olympics|Biathlon]]===
Biathlon events were conducted at the 1924 Winter Olympics under the designation [[Military patrol at the Winter Olympics|Military patrol]]. Biathlon arrived as its own sport at the 1960 Winter Olympics.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 16th by [[Anne de Besche]] in [[Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Women's sprint|women's sprint in 2026]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the sport was 54th by [[Sondre Slettemark]] in [[Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's pursuit|men's pursuit in 2026]].

===[[Bobsleigh at the Winter Olympics|Bobsleigh]]===
Bobsleigh has been included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics, with the exception of the 1960 Games.

Denmark's only placement in the sport so far is 9th, by [[Maja Voigt]] in [[Bobsleigh at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Women's monobob|women's monobob in 2026]].

===[[Cross-country skiing at the Winter Olympics|Cross-country skiing]]===
Cross-country skiing has been was included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 32nd by [[Kirsten Carlsen]] in [[Cross-country skiing at the 1968 Winter Olympics – Women's 10 kilometre|women's 10 km in 1968]].

Denmark's best placement in a men's event in the sport was 41st by [[Michael Binzer]] in both [[Cross-country skiing at the 1998 Winter Olympics – Men's 15 kilometre freestyle pursuit|men's 15 km pursuit in 1998]] and [[Cross-country skiing at the 1998 Winter Olympics – Men's 50 kilometre freestyle|men's 50 km freestyle in 1998]].

===[[Curling at the Winter Olympics|Curling]]===
Curling was included in the Olympic programme during the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics. It didn't return until 1998, but has remained in the Games since then.

[[Jane Bidstrup]], [[Helena Blach Lavrsen]], [[Dorthe Holm]], [[Margit Pörtner]] and [[Trine Qvist]] won silver in the [[Curling at the 1998 Winter Olympics|women's event in 1998]], earning Denmark's first Winter Olympic medal ever.

Denmark's best placement in a men's event is 6th, which [[Johnny Frederiksen]], [[Troels Harry]], [[Mikkel Poulsen]], [[Rasmus Stjerne]] and [[Lars Vilandt]] got in the [[Curling at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|men's event in 2014]].

===[[Figure skating at the Olympic Games|Figure skating]]===
Figure skating was first included in the Olympic programme in the 1908 and 1920 Summer Olympics. It was moved to the Winter Olympics with the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics and has been included in every Winter Olympic Games.

Denmark's best placement in the sport was 9th by [[Michael Tyllesen]] in [[Figure skating at the 1998 Winter Olympics|men's singles in 1998]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was 15th by [[Anisette Torp-Lind]] in [[Figure skating at the 1992 Winter Olympics|ladies' singles in 1992]].

===[[Freestyle skiing at the Winter Olympics|Freestyle skiing]]===
Freestyle skiing has been included in the Olympic programme since 1992.

Denmark's best placement in the sport is 13th by [[Anja Bolbjerg]] in [[Freestyle skiing at the 1998 Winter Olympics – Women's moguls|women's moguls in 1998]].

Denmark has yet to participate in men's events in the sport.

===[[Ice hockey at the Olympic Games|Ice hockey]]===
Ice hockey was first included in the Olympic programme in the 1920 Summer Olympics. It was moved to the Winter Olympics with the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics and has been included in every Winter Olympic Games.

Denmark men's and women's ice hockey teams have both competed.

[[Denmark men's national ice hockey team]]'s best placement is [[Ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|7th in 2022]].
[[Denmark women's national ice hockey team]] best placement is [[Ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Women's tournament|10th in 2022]].

===[[Skeleton at the Winter Olympics|Skeleton]]===
Skeleton has been included in the Olympic programme in 1928, 1948 and from 2002 until today.

Denmark has three placements in the sport so far.

[[Rasmus Johansen]]	finished 11th in the [[Skeleton at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's|men's event in 2026]]. 

[[Nanna Johansen]] finished 20th in the [[Skeleton at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Women's|women's event in 2026]].

Together, Rasmus Johansen and Nanna Johansen finished 12th in [[Skeleton at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Mixed team|the mixed team event in 2026]].

===[[Snowboarding at the Winter Olympics|Snowboarding]]===
Snowboarding has been included in the Olympic programme since 1998.

Denmark has competed in two snowboarding events. [[Mike Kildevæld]] finished 15th in [[Snowboarding at the 1998 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|men's giant slalom 1998]]. [[Julie Lundholdt]] finished 15th too, but in [[Snowboarding at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Women's snowboard cross|women's snowboard cross in 2010]].

===[[Speed skating at the Winter Olympics|Speed skating]]===
Speed skating has been included in the Olympic programme since the inaugural 1924 Winter Olympics.

Denmark's has won one medal in the sport; [[Viktor Hald Thorup]] won silver in [[Speed skating at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's mass start|men's mass start in 2026]].

Denmark's best placement in a women's event in the sport was 14th by [[Cathrine Grage]] in [[Speed skating at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Women's 5000 metres|women's 5000m in 2010]].

==Medals at subsequently de-recognized competitions==
[[Art competitions at the Summer Olympics|Art competitions]] held at Summer Olympics between 1912 and 1948, and the [[1906 Intercalated Games]] are no longer recognized as official Olympic medal competitions by the IOC.

Denmark won 5 silver and 4 bronze medals in art competitions,<ref name="DEN_profile" /> and 3 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze medal at the Intercalated Games.
